BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MESRA, RANCHI
(MID SEMESTER EXAMINATION)

CLASS: BE   SEMESTER: VII
BRANCH: IT   SESSION : MO/2019

                           SUBJECT : IT7041 PARALLEL AND DISTRIBUTED COMPUTING

TIME: 1.5  HOURS   FULL MARKS: 25

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. The total marks of the questions are 30.
2. Candidates may attempt for all 30 marks.
3. In those cases where the marks obtained exceed 25 marks, the excess will be ignored.
4. Before attempting the question paper, be sure that you have got the correct question paper.
5. The missing data, if any, may be assumed suitably.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Q1 (a) Define parallel processing and parallel computer. [2]
 (b) Prove that if (1/k)
th
 of the time spent executing an algorithm involves operations that
must  be  performed  sequentially,  then  an  upper  limit  on  the  speedup  achievable  by
executing the algorithm on parallel processors is k.
[3]


Q2 (a) Given a task that can be divided into m subtasks, each requiring 1 unit of time, how much
time is required for an m-stage pipeline to process n tasks?
[2]
 (b) A sequential implementation of the Sieve of Eratosthenes marks about 2.2 million cells
in  order  to  compute  all  primes  less  than  1  million.  Estimate  the  maximum  speedup
achievable by the control-parallel version of the Sieve of Eratosthenes as it finds all
primes less than 1 million.
[3]


Q3 (a) Summarize the similarities and  differences between  RAM model of serial computation
and PRAM model of parallel computation.
[2]
 (b) Prove that a p-processor PRIORITY PRAM can be simulated by a p-processor EREW PRAM
with the time complexity increased by a factor of Θ(log p).
[3]


Q4 (a) Given a one-way linked list with 15 nodes, each containing either 0 or 1, if suffix sum is
to be performed on it to rank the nodes, how many processors will be required? Estimate
the number of iteration that each of these processors will undergo while completing the
task.
[2]
 (b) Given two sorted arrays with n/2 disjoint values, how will you merge them using CREW
PRAM model? Present an algorithm to achieve the goal.
[3]


Q5 (a) What  do  you  mean  by  embedding  of  a  graph,  dilation  of embedding  and  load  of  an
embedding?
[2]
 (b) Prove that a complete binary tree of height more than 4 cannot be embedded in a 2-D
mesh without increasing the dilation beyond 1.
[3]


Q6 (a) How can be a set of active concurrent processes be deadlocked? Elaboarate. [2]
 (b) Discuss the approaches of various class of algorithms to address the problem of dynamic
load balancing on multicomputers.
[3]

BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MESRA, RANCHI
(MID SEMESTER EXAMINATION)

CLASS: BE   SEMESTER: VII
BRANCH: IT   SESSION : MO/2018

SUBJECT : IT7041 PARALLEL AND DISTRIBUTED COMPUTING

TIME: 1.5  HOURS   FULL MARKS: 25

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. The total marks of the questions are 30.
2. Candidates may attempt for all 30 marks.
3. In those cases where the marks obtained exceed 25 marks, the excess will be ignored.
4. Before attempting the question paper, be sure that you have got the correct question paper.
5. The missing data, if any, may be assumed suitably.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Q1 (a) Explain the need of parallel processing. [2]
 (b) Compare data parallelism with control parallelism. [3]

Q2 (a) Given a task that can be divided into m subtasks, each requiring 2 units of time, how
much time is required for an m-stage pipeline to process n tasks?
[2]
 (b) Prove  that  if (1/k)
th
 of  the  time spent  executing  an  algorithm  involves  operations  that
must  be  performed  sequentially,  then  an  upper  limit  on  the  speedup  achievable  by
executing the algorithm on parallel processors is k.
[3]

Q3 (a) Enumerate the features of various PRAM models of computation. [2]
 (b) Given a CREW PRAM algorithm with time complexity O(t(n)), what is an upper bound on
the time complexity of an algorithm to solve the same problem on the EREW model?
[3]

Q4 (a) Define  the  problem  of  prefix  computation.  How  can  prefix  computation  help  in
compaction? Explain with an example.
[2]
 (b) Given two sorted arrays with n/2 disjoint values, how will you merge them using CREW
PRAM model? Present an algorithm to achieve the goal.
[3]

Q5 (a)
Prove that a binomial tree of height n has a dilation  embedding in a 2-D mesh.
[2]
 (b) Prove that a complete binary tree of height more than 4 cannot be embedded in a 2-D
mesh without increasing the dilation beyond 1.
[3]
